title: One-lane finite-state transduction
statement: Let $M$ be a deterministic machine with $k$ work tapes, choose a lane $lane<k$, and let $R,C$ be types with maps $state:R\to S$ and $symbol:C\to A$ and a visit rule $visit:R\times C\to R\times C$. Suppose that whenever the selected lane reads $symbol(c)$, the transition from state $state(s)$, for any input and work-tape reads, is the single-lane action that writes $symbol$ of the updated cell, moves that lane right, and enters the state indexed by the updated register. Then, for any base configuration, word $as$ over $C$, initial register $s$, integer frontier $z$, and lists $l,r$ of optional symbols, running $M$ for $|as|$ steps from the zipper configuration whose right list begins with the encoded word $as$ followed by $r$ yields the zipper configuration whose frontier is $z+|as|$, register is the final register from the left-to-right transduction of $as$, and left list is the reversed encoded rewritten word prepended to $l$, with right list $r$.
hypotheses_covered: $M$ is a deterministic machine with $k$ work tapes
the transition condition $htr$ holds for every $s,c,inp,ws$ with the selected lane reading $symbol(c)$
$l,r$ are finite lists of optional symbols
replaced:
Suppose a machine's transitions, on a family of control states indexed by a
register type, always perform a right-moving single-lane write determined by a
local visit function of the register and the symbol read on the designated
lane.  Then running the machine for exactly the length of a word laid out on
that lane's zipper computes the left fold of the visit function over the word:
the final control carries the folded register, the frontier advances by the
word's length, the processed stack holds the rewritten word reversed, and all
inactive tapes are unchanged.
